articles.title: Baird downgrades Nvidia on China curbs, AI demand worries
articles.desc: Baird downgraded Nvidia's stock and cut its price target significantly due to various market risks. Concerns over US restrictions on chip sales to China have emerged, affecting Nvidia's revenue outlook. Demand for Nvidia's chips is showing signs of softening amid supply constraints and market uncertainties. Additionally, multiple brokerages have removed Nvidia from their top picks due to recent stock declines.

articles.title: EasyJet shareholders approve £5.7 billion Apollo takeover
articles.desc: EasyJet's shareholders voted to approve a £5.7 billion takeover by Apollo on Wednesday. This decision marks a major step towards removing EasyJet from the London stock market. With 97.07% of scheme shares in favor, the airline is targeting a deal completion by the first quarter of next year. Nonetheless, the takeover faces regulatory scrutiny in the EU regarding airline ownership rules.

articles.title: India to switch bonds worth 250 billion rupees next week
articles.desc: On November 16, the Reserve Bank of India will initiate a significant switch auction worth 250 billion rupees. This maneuver involves replacing six bonds that are set to mature between 2027 and 2029 with longer-term securities extending to maturity in 2062. By doing so, the government seeks to optimize its debt repayment schedule. This follows a similar strategy of bond buyback and issuance enacted in October.

articles.title: Dollar firms as hot inflation, hawkish Fed talk lift rate-hike bets

Inflation data revealed an increase in consumer prices, prompting trader speculation about further monetary tightening. The Japanese yen has weakened to its lowest level in over two months, approaching significant mark. Many developed-market currencies are performing poorly against the dollar this year, attributed to widening interest-rate gaps.

articles.title: India blocked 129 betting websites on basis of fake high court orders: Report

Investigations have been initiated after it was revealed that these court orders were fake. The Rajasthan and Allahabad High Courts confirmed that the supposed orders did not exist in their records. Concerns about the authenticity of legal documents are growing due to technology advancements.

The proposed benchmark price is linked to wage movements and consumer price indices, which will be reviewed periodically. Producers believe this pricing mechanism will help absorb wage increases and support investment in tea production.
